title: Optimize walkthrough - quant profiles INT8/FP8 - quality vs latency (Stratus AI)
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on INT8 and FP8 quantization profiles, demo of quality vs latency dashboards, discussion of benchmark numbers for Stratus AI's 6B conversational model. Customer requested benchmark spreadsheet, pilot scope, and security docs. Next steps: send bench template, schedule pilot kickoff, follow up on private deployment requirements.
next_steps: Alex: Share benchmark spreadsheet and pilot pricing (due 2026-11-15)
Priya: Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-11-23
Maya: Provide eval prompt set and 1k sample logs by 2026-11-18
Owen: Confirm VPC peering requirements and KMS provider details
action_items: Alex (AE): Send pilot pricing + benchmark template by 2026-11-15
Priya (SE): Run initial INT8/FP8 run on Redwood test infra and share results by 2026-11-19
Maya (VP ML): Share eval prompt set (1k) by 2026-11-18
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'll do a quick intro then hand off to Priya for the Optimize walkthrough.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Hi thanks, Maya here, VP ML at Stratus, we run a 6B convo model for support/assist, very sensitive to latency but also quality.
[00:23] Alex Morgan: Great, goal today is to show INT8 vs FP8 profiles and how quality vs latency looks in the Console/Optimize dashboards and talk about pilot.
[00:35] Priya Shah: OK jumping in, first slide shows baseline - fp16 at our default settings, average p95 latency 240ms on our benchmark (6B, 512 tokens), cost baseline is X, quality metric on our eval suite is 0.92 exact-match-ish, quick note transcription hiccup sometimes reads KV cache as K V cash in logs.
[01:05] Owen Price: Quick Q - when you say p95 240ms that's hosted or dedicated?
[01:10] Priya Shah: These numbers are on hosted with our optimized kernels, so cloud hosts, can be lower on dedicated because we pin to GPUs and tune queueing; for dedicated you'll see a 5-15% latency drop typically.
[01:25] Rina Gupta: How does INT8 compare? We've looked at int8 in-house and saw drop in quality on some instruction-following prompts.
[01:33] Priya Shah: Right - INT8 usually gives the biggest win on throughput and cost, about 1.9-2.4x token throughput depending on sequence length, and latency improves p50/p95 by ~20-35% over fp16 for our 6B profile. Quality delta is workload-dependent; on our standard eval set we saw a 1.5-3% drop in NLI/accuracy-style metrics for INT8, but for many dialogue completions it's smaller.
[02:05] Maya Chen: And FP8? we've been hearing about FP8 being a good middle ground.
[02:09] Priya Shah: FP8 (our FP8-mixed profile) tends to keep quality very close to fp16, like 0.5% or less degradation on most metrics, with latency improvements of ~10-20% and cost ~1.3-1.6x improvement. It's often recommended when you care about preserving quality while still getting cost/latency wins.
[02:37] Diego Ramos: demo time - opening the Optimize dashboard - you can see plotted quality vs latency across profiles, each point is a quant-profile run, this is real run data we did on Stratus-like model. Notice the orange cluster (INT8) pushes far left on latency but down a bit on quality; blue (FP8) sits closer to baseline quality with moderate latency win.
[03:05] Rina Gupta: The dashboard shows confidence intervals - how many runs per profile?
[03:10] Priya Shah: We run 5 seeds typically with varying batch/sequence distributions to estimate variance; we also recommend customers run a holdout eval set provided by them to detect edge cases.
[03:22] Owen Price: For production, we need regression alerts and the ability to roll back automatically if quality drops. Does Redwood support that?
[03:29] Priya Shah: Yes - Optimize integrates with our rollouts: you can canary an INT8 profile to 10% traffic, monitor quality metrics tied to your eval prompts, and auto-fallback to fp16 or FP8 if thresholds cross. We keep request-level traces and evaluation hooks.
[03:45] Maya Chen: Data residency / encryption question - if we run dedicated or private, how do you handle keys?
[03:51] Alex Morgan: For Private we support customer KMS/HSM, and all logs can be disabled or forwarded to your SIEM, we also offer SOC 2 docs, ISO packs are in the security folder; we'll send the security packet after.
[04:06] Maya Chen: Great. Also curious about model variants - can you route to a smaller quantized variant for cheaper queries?
[04:12] Priya Shah: Yep, smart routing supports policy-based routing — cost-first vs latency-first, region-based; we can fallback to a quantized variant or different model family if SLOs are in danger.
[04:24] Rina Gupta: One nit - we've seen hallucinations increase slightly with INT8 on multi-step reasoning flows. Is that typical?
[04:30] Priya Shah: It can happen; that's why we run per-prompt evals and fine-grained thresholds. Sometimes a small prompt re-write or a tiny temperature adjustment mitigates it. For high-risk flows we often recommend FP8 first, then pilot INT8 on low-risk traffic.
[04:49] Maya Chen: What's the pilot look like - timelines and deliverables?
[04:52] Alex Morgan: Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: week 1 gather evals and sample logs + run initial bench, week 2 iterate quant profiles and produce a cost/latency/quality matrix, week 3 canary on traffic for a small slice and validate regen, week 4 finalize rollout plan. We'll provide the bench template and an automatic runner if you want.
[05:15] Owen Price: Any infra prerequisites for Private? network peering, subnet rules?
[05:19] Alex Morgan: For Private we need VPC peering, port ranges for the control plane if you use hosted control plane (optional), and KMS endpoints. We'll share a checklist.
[05:30] Priya Shah: Back to numbers - here's a concrete example from our run: fp16 p95 240ms, FP8 p95 190ms (20% improvement), INT8 p95 150ms (37% improvement). Quality scores: fp16 0.92, FP8 0.915, INT8 0.89 on the holdout. Those deltas match the typical pattern.
[06:00] Maya Chen: 0.89 seems a bit low for us on critical queries.
[06:03] Priya Shah: Understood. We can focus INT8 on less critical endpoints (embeddings, rerank, background tasks) and keep FP8 or fp16 for customer-facing decision flows. Also, we can do layer-wise quantization tuning to recover some quality for INT8.
[06:25] Rina Gupta: How do you validate token-level diffs? We need an audit trail for regressions.
[06:29] Diego Ramos: Optimize stores diffs and can snapshot responses for a given prompt set; we also integrate with your eval harness so you can reproduce runs. Audit logs are exportable.
[06:40] Maya Chen: Pricing - how do you price quant profiles? is it per-token discounted?
[06:44] Alex Morgan: Pricing is usage-based; quantized profiles are priced lower per-token relative to fp16, we give example multipliers in the pricing sheet we'll send — pilot customers often get a committed discount.
[06:57] Owen Price: Any red flags if we want to do on-prem GPU cluster? we have DGX boxes, do you support that?
[07:04] Priya Shah: Yes, Private on-prem is supported; we ship an on-prem package, you keep model weights and keys, and our control plane can be customer-hosted. There are some kernel tuning steps per GPU generation, our SEs will help.
[07:18] Maya Chen: OK want to call out a few follow-ups: we want the bench template, security docs, and a recommendation whether to pilot FP8 vs INT8 first.
[07:27] Alex Morgan: Actionable - we'll send bench template and security packet; recommendation from today: start with FP8 for customer-facing flows, INT8 for background/low-risk routes.
[07:36] Priya Shah: Also note for the pilot we'll instrument a set of regression alerts in Optimize and provide a daily digest.
[07:44] Maya Chen: Sounds good, thanks.
[07:46] Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and target dates.
[07:50] (end)
